title: Infosys Slides After Guidance Cut as AI Deflation Weighs on Growth
excerpt: India's second-largest IT services firm trimmed its FY27 revenue forecast for the second straight quarter, with AI-led pricing pressure offsetting strong deal wins and a smooth CEO succession announcement.
body:
• Infosys cut its FY27 constant currency revenue growth guidance to 1.5%–3.0%, down from 1.5%–3.5%, with organic growth guidance at -0.2% to 1.3%.
  • Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% year-on-year to ₹48,211 crore while net profit climbed 12.2% to ₹7,769 crore, though both missed analyst estimates.
  • The company named 30-year veteran Ashiss Kumar Dash as CEO-designate, set to succeed Salil Parekh from April 1, 2027.
  • JPMorgan downgraded the stock to Neutral, while multiple brokerages cut target prices, citing AI-led pricing deflation and subdued discretionary spending.

Infosys shares came under pressure after the Bengaluru-based IT services giant reported a softer-than-expected June quarter and cut its full-year revenue growth forecast for the second consecutive quarter. The stock fell over 2% on the NSE following the results, hitting a low of ₹1,013.90 before closing at ₹1,040.90.

Revenue Misses, Profit Falls Short

Revenue for Q1 FY27 rose 14% year-on-year and 3.9% sequentially to ₹48,211 crore ($4.99 billion), missing LSEG-compiled analyst estimates of ₹48,367 crore. Net profit climbed 12.2% year-on-year to ₹7,769 crore but fell 8.6% from the March quarter, again below the consensus forecast of ₹7,832 crore.

The company narrowed its full-year constant currency revenue growth guidance to 1.5%–3.0%, lowering the upper end from the earlier 3.5%. Stripping out acquisitions, organic growth guidance now stands at -0.2% to 1.3% — a sharp slowdown that would require quarterly sequential growth of 0.4%–1.4% in a challenging demand environment, according to JPMorgan.

AI: Growth Engine and Revenue Headwind

AI revenue now accounts for 8.2% of Infosys's quarterly revenue and is growing at a double-digit rate sequentially. Large deal total contract value (TCV) rose to $3.6 billion from $3.2 billion in the preceding quarter, driven partly by AI-related engagements.

But the flip side is clear: AI-led productivity gains are compressing pricing on existing contracts, sometimes even mid-engagement. JPMorgan noted that strong deal signings have yet to translate into revenue because of this AI-driven pricing pressure. An unexpected client contract termination in the Energy, Utilities, Resources and Services (EURS) vertical and challenges with the Daimler contract added to the revenue drag.

"AI momentum is now rapidly converting into revenue, which demonstrates how Infosys' differentiated enterprise AI value proposition is translating into consistent market share gains."

— Salil Parekh, CEO, Infosys

CEO Succession

Alongside the results, Infosys announced Ashiss Kumar Dash as CEO-designate, effective immediately. Dash, a three-decade company veteran who currently heads the EURS vertical, will succeed Salil Parekh as CEO and Managing Director from April 1, 2027, when Parekh's second term ends. The board said Dash was selected by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, marking the first formal internal succession in several years.

Analysts broadly welcomed the choice, noting that an internal appointment should provide leadership continuity. Centrum Broking and 360 ONE Capital cautioned, however, that the stock may remain under pressure until investors gain clarity on Dash's strategic direction.

Brokerages Mixed, Targets Cut

JPMorgan downgraded Infosys to Neutral with a target price of ₹1,050, calling the quarter a sharp miss and noting multiple headwinds to growth momentum. Jefferies held at Hold and cut its target to ₹1,020 from ₹1,235. Morgan Stanley maintained Equal Weight and reduced its target to ₹1,075 from ₹1,112.

BofA was more constructive, maintaining Buy but cutting its target to ₹1,300 from ₹1,570, highlighting strong AI execution and deal momentum. Motilal Oswal kept a Buy with a ₹1,170 target, while Elara Capital downgraded to Accumulate from Buy, slashing its target to ₹1,150 from ₹1,530 and cutting earnings estimates by 4%–6%.

Operating margin held at 21.1%, within the full-year guidance range of 20%–22%. CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka pointed to disciplined execution and strong cash generation as buffers against near-term revenue pressure.

What's Next

Infosys plans to build a team of 6,000 frontier AI engineers over the coming years as it bets on AI services as the primary growth driver. Salary hikes will roll out in two phases — October for most employees, January for senior levels. With the sector broadly under pressure from AI disruption and subdued client spending, the near-term growth path remains uncertain despite robust deal pipelines.
nri_angle: Infosys is one of the largest employers and investment vehicles for the Indian diaspora; its performance directly affects NRI portfolios and the IT sector workforce.
